recommendations.text: Chest radiography should be obtained to confirm diagnosis
For CAP Initial Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - assess vital signs - assess respiratory status - order imaging chest xray (within 60 minutes) - order lab cbc
Penicillin anaphylaxis precludes all penicillin-class antibiotics. [FORBIDDEN: give_amoxicillin, give_ampicillin, give_piperacillin] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Fluoroquinolones prolong QT interval, risking torsades de pointes. [FORBIDDEN: give_levofloxacin, give_moxifloxacin, give_fluoroquinolone] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ATS/IDSA CAP 2019; FDA Black Box Warning

recommendations.text: Severe CAP requiring ICU needs combination antibiotic therapy. [REQUIRED: give_beta_lactam_plus_macrolide, give_beta_lactam_plus_fluoroquinolone] (Severity: HIGH)
MRSA risk factors require empiric MRSA coverage. [REQUIRED: add_vancomycin, add_linezolid] (Severity: HIGH)

MRSA-risk patients (prior MRSA, cavitary infiltrate) require vancomycin or linezolid; standard empiric therapy is insufficient. [FORBIDDEN: give_standard_empiric_without_mrsa_in_risk, omit_vancomycin_or_linezolid_in_mrsa_risk] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ATS/IDSA CAP 2019; MRSA CAP has 30-40% mortality without appropriate coverage

recommendations.text: Pseudomonas risk factors require antipseudomonal coverage. [REQUIRED: give_antipseudomonal_beta_lactam] (Severity: HIGH)

Pseudomonas-risk patients need antipseudomonal coverage; standard CAP empiric or single-agent therapy leads to treatment failure. [FORBIDDEN: give_non_antipseudomonal_in_risk, give_single_agent_for_pseudomonas_risk] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ATS/IDSA CAP 2019; Pseudomonas CAP requires antipseudomonal agents; standard empiric monotherapy is inadequate

recommendations.text: Immunocompromised patients need broader coverage including PJP, fungal, atypical. [FORBIDDEN: give_standard_cap_antibiotics_only, delay_empiric_coverage] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ATS/IDSA CAP 2019, Section 6; IDSA Immunocompromised Host 2013

recommendations.text: Aspiration risk requires anaerobic coverage. [REQUIRED: add_anaerobic_coverage] (Severity: MODERATE)

Aspiration pneumonia involves anaerobes that macrolides don't cover; omitting anaerobic coverage leads to treatment failure. [FORBIDDEN: give_azithromycin_only_for_aspiration, omit_anaerobic_coverage_in_aspiration] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ATS/IDSA CAP 2019; aspiration pneumonia involves polymicrobial anaerobes requiring specific coverage

recommendations.text: Steroids in COVID-CAP only if hypoxic. Steroids without O2 need increase mortality. [FORBIDDEN: give_steroid_without_oxygen_requirement, give_high_dose_steroid_early] (Severity: HIGH)
Severe CAP with hemodynamic instability or respiratory failure requires ICU. [REQUIRED: admit_to_icu, give_iv_antibiotics_immediately] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Severe CAP meeting ICU criteria (shock, respiratory failure) must not be managed on general ward; delays worsen mortality. [FORBIDDEN: treat_on_ward_if_severe_cap, delay_icu_transfer_in_severe_cap] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ATS/IDSA CAP 2019; severe CAP (PaO2/FiO2 < 250, multilobar, septic shock) requires ICU-level care

recommendations.text: Beta-lactam plus macrolide or respiratory fluoroquinolone for inpatient non-ICU CAP
For Inpatient CAP Management, the following actions are mandatory: - order lab blood culture - give beta lactam plus macrolide (within 240 minutes)
Administer antibiotics as soon as possible, ideally within 1 hour for severe CAP
For Severe CAP / ICU, the following actions are mandatory: - order lab blood culture - give beta lactam plus macrolide (within 60 minutes) - assess icu criteria - give iv fluids
During Severe CAP / ICU, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay antibiotics for cultures beyond 1h.
